On October 15, 1794, the Philadelphia Mint delivered 1,758 silver dollars, struck on a hand-turned screw press. It was the only day of dollar production that year.

These Flowing Hair dollars were the first silver dollars issued by the United States. Fewer than 200 are believed to survive.

The finest known example is unusual. A small silver plug was added to its blank at the Mint to bring it up to standard weight, and some experts believe it may be the very first silver dollar struck.

In 1947 the coin changed hands for $1,250. On January 24, 2013, at a Stack's Bowers Galleries auction in New York, it sold for $10,016,875. It was the first coin ever to top $10 million at auction.

🔊 From Gaza to Minab, Children’s dreams buried under rubble and bombardment

📌 Tehran, IRNA – World Children’s Day comes as thousands of children in Palestine, Lebanon, Yemen and Iran have lost their lives in military attacks, while many others have been injured, displaced or deprived of education and a safe childhood.

World Children’s Day arrived as more than 21,700 Palestinian children have been killed and over 45,000 injured in Gaza since the war began in October 2023.
​
The destruction of schools and hospitals, repeated displacement and shortages of food and clean water have further worsened their living conditions.
​
Many have lost their homes and families, while others have been forced to grow up amid fear, hunger and the constant threat of Israeli bombardment instead of having a normal childhood.
​
Lebanon has also witnessed a heavy toll on children, with more than 316 killed and 1,450 injured since October 2023.
​
Israeli airstrikes during the latest escalation in 2026 killed dozens more, including 33 children in a single day.
​
Many of these children were killed or injured while at home or in their communities, far from any battlefield, losing the safety and innocence that should define childhood.
​
Years of conflict and economic hardship in Yemen have left children facing malnutrition, lack of education and inadequate healthcare.
​
The situation has been further worsened by US airstrikes, which have also claimed the lives of children.
​
At least two children, aged six and eight, were among those killed in US airstrikes on Saada Province in March 2025.
​
These children, who had no role in the conflict, became victims of military attacks while already struggling to survive years of hardship.
​
One of the deadliest attacks on children in Iran was the strike on Shajareh Tayyebeh elementary school in Minab on February 28, 2026.
​
120 children were among the 156 people killed in the attack, which took place during the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.
​
The students had gone to school to learn and spend time with their classmates, carrying schoolbags and books rather than having any role in the conflict.
​
Many families who had sent their children to school that morning never saw them return home.
​
The suffering of children across the region raises questions about the effectiveness of international mechanisms to protect them and prevent them from becoming victims of military aggression.
​
Children, regardless of where they live, have the same right to life, safety and a future free from war.
​
World Children’s Day is observed annually on November 20, marking the adoption of the Declaration of the Rights of the Child in 1959 and the Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1989 by the United Nations General Assembly.

Prime Minister Netanyahu is reportedly convinced that Iran is accelerating its preparations for biological and chemical warfare. The CIA is said to have corroborated that assessment, and the U.S. president publicly warned Iran today against using such weapons on American soil.

My concern is that Iran could still resort to using them against Israel or elsewhere in the Middle East.

As a student and teacher of Bible prophecy, I keep coming back to two things in Ezekiel 38:

On the eve of the war Ezekiel describes, Israel is living securely and prospering.
Iran, identified as Persia in the prophecy, comes against Israel as part of a broader coalition.

When I put those two things together and look at what is happening today, I believe Israel may strike Iran and severely weaken its military capabilities. I expect the IRGC would survive. A ground invasion aimed at toppling the regime is unlikely to be on the table.

Given the political uncertainty in Israel, my guess is that the window for such a strike could be as short as 14 to 21 days.

I am not a prophet. If I had to venture a guess, I would say that the United States will give Israel the green light while staying out of the strike itself. If Iran’s military is severely weakened, the regime may then agree to a deal that allows it to survive.

That is my reading of current events in light of Bible prophecy. The timing and the sequence are my own speculation.

Whatever happens, the Word of God will prove true. So spend more time in His Word than you do reading analyses like mine. In His Word you will find wisdom, comfort, and peace.

Awaiting His Soon Return,
